papers.title: Machine Learning of Linear Differential Equations using Gaussian Processes
papers.abstract: This work leverages recent advances in probabilistic machine learning to discover conservation laws expressed by parametric linear equations. Such equations involve, but are not limited to, ordinary and partial differential, integro-differential, and fractional order operators. Here, Gaussian process priors are modified according to the particular form of such operators and are employed to infer parameters of the linear equations from scarce and possibly noisy observations. Such observations may come from experiments or "black-box" computer simulations.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该方法使用高斯过程推断线性微分方程参数，提供不确定性量化，但未涉及有限元代理模型或生物力学设计，仅提供背景方法参考。
llm.why_not_core: Does not involve FEA surrogate modeling, no mechanics/implants context, no handling of constraints or sampling efficiency for simulations.

summary_zh.motivation: 从稀疏有噪数据中发现线性微分方程的守恒律
summary_zh.method: 根据线性算子修改高斯过程先验，推断方程参数
summary_zh.result: 能从少量观测中恢复参数，具有不确定性量化
summary_zh.validation: 未明确指定验证，理论上适用

summary_en.motivation: To discover conservation laws expressed by parametric linear differential equations from scarce and noisy observations.
summary_en.method: Gaussian process priors are modified according to the linear operator to infer the parameters of the equations.
summary_en.result: The method infers parameters from scarce observations, providing uncertainty quantification.
summary_en.validation: Validation is theoretical, not explicitly demonstrated on specific problems.

papers.title: 3D bioprinting of GelMA scaffolds triggers mineral deposition by primary human osteoblasts.
papers.abstract: Due to its relatively low level of antigenicity and high durability, titanium has successfully been used as the major material for biological implants. However, because the typical interface between titanium and tissue precludes adequate transmission of load into the surrounding bone, over time, load-bearing implants tend to loosen and revision surgeries are required. Osseointegration of titanium implants requires presentation of both biological and mechanical cues that promote attachment of and trigger mineral deposition by osteoblasts. While many factors contribute to differentiation, the relative importance of the various cues is unclear. To substantially improve osseointegration of titanium implants, we generated a gelatin methacryloyl (GelMA) scaffold, using an extrusion-based 3D bioprinter, which can be directly printed on and grafted to the titanium implant surface. We demonstrate that this scaffold is able to trigger mineral deposition of both MG63 osteoblasts and primary normal human osteoblasts in the absence of any exogenous osteogenic factors. Films of the same formulation failed to promote mineral deposition suggesting that the three dimensional scaffold was able to tip the balance in favor of differentiation despite other potentially unfavorable differentiation cues of the material. We further show that these GelMA lattices can be directly grafted to titanium alloy and are secure in vitro over a period of seven weeks. When grafted within a groove system, the GelMA hydrogel is protected from shearing forces in a marrow implantation model. This prepares the way for osteogenic coatings to be directly manufactured on the implant surface and packaged for surgery.
papers.first_author_affiliation: Center for Manufacturing Innovation, Fraunhofer USA, Brookline, MA 02446, USA.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文涉及生物打印，但未使用任何人工智能或机器学习方法。
llm.why_not_core: The paper does not incorporate any AI/ML method into the bioprinting workflow; it is purely experimental bioprinting without computational modeling.

summary_zh.motivation: 改善钛植入物的骨整合，用生物打印支架促进矿物沉积。
summary_zh.method: 在钛表面3D打印GelMA支架，培养成骨细胞无骨诱导因子。
summary_zh.result: 支架在体外触发矿物沉积，而薄膜不能。
summary_zh.validation: 通过原代成骨细胞和MG63细胞体外培养验证。

summary_en.motivation: To improve osseointegration of titanium implants by using a bioprinted scaffold that promotes mineral deposition from osteoblasts.
summary_en.method: GelMA scaffolds were extrusion-printed directly onto titanium and cultured with primary human osteoblasts in the absence of osteogenic factors.
summary_en.result: The 3D scaffold, but not a film, triggered mineral deposition in vitro.
summary_en.validation: In vitro cell culture with primary normal human osteoblasts and MG63 cells, confirmed by mineral deposition assays.
